root.claim: One fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies n-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Beat the $n\log n$ cost of transform-based multiplication by making the two tape operations (address rearrangement and butterfly layers) cost a power of their width less than a full scan, then plug them into the Harvey-van der Hoeven resampling reduction

motivation.text: Scanning the data once per transform level already costs n log n, so savings are needed in both movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a power of the logarithm, with an astronomically small but fixed exponent kappa=2^-182.
